narrative_purpose: Anchors the cold open: the decisive instant of a single hunt, the prey breaking as the pack closes, before any theory arrives. The reader watches one chase so the system underneath it can be revealed.
subject: A single small six-limbed browser caught mid-stride, body twisting to bolt, the bright fan of skin on its skull thrown fully open to show a startling pattern of false eyes. Four sleek black six-limbed pack-hunters fan out in a half-circle around it, low and fast, one already lunging from the left, the others cutting off escape to the right. All five animals carry faint glowing markings along their flanks.
scene: Dense bioluminescent night forest, glowing ferns and root-buttresses, tall trunks vanishing into haze, motes of spore-light disturbed by the motion.
camera: Dynamic low three-quarter action view, slight motion energy, the prey near centre with hunters sweeping in from the edges.
light: Glowing undergrowth throws the brightest light upward, catching the flared fan and the prey's straining muscles; the hunters read as rim-lit shadows with glinting eyes.
palette: Cool teal-indigo dominant, prey lifted in cyan, hunters in near-black with cyan edges, the eyespot fan carrying a single scarce warm magenta accent.
style: Hand-painted naturalist action plate of real alien animals, textured brushwork, not a film still.
detail_level: High on the prey and the flared fan and the nearest hunter; softer on the trailing hunters and hazy forest.
composition: Converging diagonals of hunters from both sides onto the bright twisting prey, open dark forest depth behind for breathing room.
consistency_notes: Same viperwolf and hexapede archetypes as fig-00-cover; keep the sleek six-limbed black hunters and the small six-legged fan-crested browser consistent.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no UI chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
